paper_metadata.title: An Empirical Study on Enhancing Explainability through Quantum Machine Learning for Credit Risk Analysis

summary: The paper studies gate-based quantum machine learning for credit score classification using QSVC with ZZFeatureMap, PauliFeatureMap, and a combined ZZPauliMap. It reports classical SVC accuracy of about 79.0% before tuning and 78.7% after tuning, while the quantum model achieves 75.7% with individual feature maps and up to 84.8% with the combined ZZPauliMap after cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning.

experiments.description: Quantum support vector classification for credit score classification using quantum feature maps (ZZFeatureMap, PauliFeatureMap, and combined ZZPauliMap) with QSVC, compared against classical SVC baseline.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC) with ZZFeatureMap, PauliFeatureMap, and ZZPauliMap
algorithm.convergence_criteria: stratified k-fold cross-validation and grid search hyperparameter tuning; no explicit stopping criterion reported

problem_formulation.objective_function: Credit score classification / binary or multiclass classification of credit risk classes using QSVC decision boundary in quantum feature space

Classical SVC baseline is reported in the paper and is not treated as a separate experiment.
The paper reports classical SVC accuracy of about 79.0% and 78.7%, while QSVC reaches 75.7% with individual feature maps and 78.7% to 84.8% with the combined ZZPauliMap after tuning.

Because the best reported quantum accuracy matches or slightly exceeds the classical baseline, but no runtime or scaling evidence is provided, this is best treated as parity/limited empirical improvement rather than demonstrated practical advantage.
